title: The History of Need for Speed | Underground, Most Wanted, Hot Pursuit and More
description: How Need for Speed went from a 1994 exotic-car racer to a street racing legend: Underground, Most Wanted, Criterion's Hot Pursuit and Unbound explained.

sections.heading: A racing legend
sections.script: Need for Speed is one of the most famous racing series in gaming. It has given us exotic supercars, police chases, neon-lit street races and some of the best car soundtracks ever. In this video we go through the history of the series, from the very first game in nineteen ninety four, to Underground and Most Wanted, the return of Hot Pursuit, and the latest game, Unbound. If you ever spent a night racing in Rockport or Olympic City, stay with us.
images: wiki:Need for Speed: Most Wanted (2005 video game)

sections.heading: Nineteen ninety four: the beginning
sections.script: The first game, simply called The Need for Speed, was released in nineteen ninety four. It was developed by Electronic Arts Canada and published by Electronic Arts. Instead of arcade-style fantasy, it focused on driving real exotic cars on scenic roads, a simple idea that gave the whole series its thrill. From that first game, the series has grown into one of the most successful racing franchises of all time.
images: wiki:Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit (2010 video game)

sections.heading: Police chases arrive
sections.script: As the series grew, one idea kept coming back: the police chase. Need for Speed three, called Hot Pursuit, arrived in nineteen ninety eight, and let you play as either the racer or the cop. Chasing or escaping the police became a signature of the series, and most games that followed included police pursuits in some form. In two thousand two, a new team called EA Black Box took over the series with Hot Pursuit two, and that move would change everything.
images: wiki:Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit (2010 video game)

sections.heading: Two thousand three: Underground
sections.script: Then came Need for Speed Underground in two thousand three. It moved the whole series from exotic supercars on scenic roads to illegal street racing in a city at night, with tuner cars, neon lights and deep customisation. It introduced drifting and drag racing to the series, and it let you change how your car looked as well as how it performed. For a whole generation of players, Underground was the game that made them fall in love with car modding.
images: wiki:Need for Speed: Most Wanted (2005 video game)

sections.heading: Two thousand five: Most Wanted
sections.script: In two thousand five, Need for Speed Most Wanted brought the police back into the spotlight. The story was built around the Blacklist, a crew of fifteen racers that you had to beat one by one to climb to the top. Each rival unlocked new parts, cars and tracks, and the police chases across the city were tense and exciting. Many fans still call it the best Need for Speed ever made, and it remains a favourite among fans.
images: wiki:Need for Speed: Most Wanted (2005 video game)

sections.heading: Two thousand ten: Criterion and Hot Pursuit
sections.script: In two thousand ten, the British studio Criterion Games took over and delivered a new Hot Pursuit. It was a successor to the nineteen ninety eight game of the same name, and it introduced Autolog, a social system that let you track your progress, compare your times on leaderboards and share screenshots with friends. The game was well received by critics, and a remastered version was released ten years later, in twenty twenty.
images: wiki:Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit (2010 video game)

sections.heading: Different styles over the years
sections.script: Not every game followed the same recipe. Over the years the series has also tried simulation racing with the Shift games, a mobile free-to-play game called No Limits in twenty fifteen, and many different studios, including EA Canada, EA Black Box, Slightly Mad Studios, Criterion and Ghost Games. Each team brought its own style, which is why fans often argue about which era was the best.
images: wiki:Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit (2010 video game)

sections.heading: Unbound: the latest chapter
sections.script: The most recent game in the series is Need for Speed Unbound, released on December second, twenty twenty two. Developed by Criterion, it brings street racing back to the centre of the series. It carries forward the idea that began with Underground: your car is your identity, and how it looks matters as much as how fast it goes.

sections.heading: Your favourite Need for Speed
sections.script: That was the history of Need for Speed, from exotic cars in nineteen ninety four to the street racing of Unbound. Now it is your turn. Which Need for Speed game is your favourite: Underground, Most Wanted, Hot Pursuit, or something else? Tell us in the comments below, and subscribe to the channel for more gaming history, guides and news.
